_: I-15, the credentials map. What a degree or a certificate actually covers, so a CV that names one is credited with the skills behind it instead of only the words written on the page. Every entry is drafted from the official body of knowledge or course outline named in 'source'; 'topics' holds that official text, and 'covers' is only ever filled from it by tools/draft_credentials.js, which keeps the skills our own dictionary knows and drops the rest. A person reads the draft, moves anything doubtful from core to side or deletes it, and sets 'checked' to their name and the date. Nothing with checked = false is used on the site.

rules.certificate_core: counts as a Match: you were examined on it
rules.certificate_side: counts as a Close (half): it is in the syllabus but not what the certificate is about
rules.degree_core: counts as a Close (half): you sat the courses, you were not certified on the skill

entries.name: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt

source.name: ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Body of Knowledge (2022)

entries.topics: DMAIC DMADV IDOV. FMEA design FMEA process FMEA RPN. Lean: theory of constraints, value chain, flow, takt time, just-in-time, gemba, spaghetti diagram. Value stream mapping. SMART goals, KPIs, scorecards. SIPOC. Benchmarking. Voice of the customer, surveys, focus groups, interviews. QFD, CTQ tree, Kano model. Project charter, process maps, Pareto charts. Work breakdown structure, Gantt charts, critical path method, PERT. Affinity diagram, tree diagram, prioritization matrix, SWOT analysis. DPU, RTY, cost of poor quality, DPMO, sigma level, process capability. RACI, brainstorming, nominal group technique. Flowcharts. Probability, central limit theorem. Normal, binomial, Poisson, chi square, t and F distributions. Sampling, random sampling, stratified sampling, check sheets, data collection. Descriptive statistics. Scatter diagram, histogram, box plot, normal probability plot. Measurement system analysis, gauge R and R, bias, linearity. Process capability indices Cp Cpk Pp Ppk. Multi-vari study. Correlation and linear regression. Hypothesis testing, t test, F test, ANOVA, chi square test. Gap analysis. Root cause analysis, cause and effect diagram, 5 whys, fault tree analysis. Design of experiments, main effects, interaction. Proof of concept, pilot test. Waste elimination, pull system, kanban, 5S, standard work, poka-yoke. Cycle time reduction, continuous flow, setup reduction, SMED. Kaizen. Statistical process control, control charts, X bar R chart, p chart, c chart. Control plan, document control, training plan. Audits. PDCA. Total productive maintenance, predictive maintenance. Visual factory, andon, jidoka.

covers.from: Voice of the customer, surveys, focus groups
Pareto, Root cause analysis, cause and effect diagram
Work breakdown structure, Gantt, critical path

drop.Healthcare and clinical: matched RPN, which means Risk Priority Number here, not Registered Practical Nurse
drop.Marketing: matched benchmarking and SWOT; the certificate is not about marketing
drop.Assembly: matched takt time and cycle time; that is not assembly work

covers.from: Voice of the customer, surveys, focus groups
measurement system analysis, DPMO, sigma level

statistical process control, Statistical process control, control charts

_review: 'drop' lists what a reviewer took out of the draft and why; those lines stay in the file so a later run cannot quietly put them back. 'all_side' marks a credential whose skills are all half credit. 'includes' means this credential also covers everything another one does.
draft_note: Every entry is signed, so draft_mode is off: the site uses the entries themselves, not drafts.
_degrees: A degree is recognised by a degree word and its subject on the same line of the education section (field_words), not by a phrase written one exact way: a CV saying 'Bachelor of Engineering, Mechanical' means the same as 'B.Eng. Mechanical Engineering'.
_signature: Each entry carries the name of the person who read it and the day they read it, and the source it was read against. A signature belongs to that version of the official syllabus: when the body that issues the credential revises it, the entry goes back in the queue to be read again. A signature is also dropped whenever the set of skills an entry covers changes - not when the dictionary is merely rebuilt, which would turn reviewing into a chore and then into a rubber stamp.
